entities.summary: Raymond Earl Baldwin was an American politician who served as a United States senator from Connecticut and also as the 72nd and 74th governor of Connecticut. A conservative Republican, he was elected governor of Connecticut in 1938 during a Republican landslide promising a balanced budget, government aid to private business, and lower taxes. He sharply cut the state budget, producing a million dollars surplus. He was defeated for reelection in 1940, but was elected governor again in 1942 and 1944.
